title: Grace and Reinstatement Periods Written into the Ridgecrest RxSecure Plans
content:
Two periods are written into each Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan and vary with the plan held. The premium grace period is the run of calendar days after the first unpaid premium charge before involuntary termination may be processed. The reinstatement window is the run of calendar days after the coverage end date within which a good-cause reinstatement may still be requested.

| Plan | Premium grace period (calendar days) | Reinstatement window after the coverage end date (calendar days) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Basic (PDP) | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Value (PDP) | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Select (PDP) | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Plus (PDP) | 90 | 60 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Complete (PDP) | 120 | 90 |
| Ridgecrest RxSecure Premier (PDP) | 120 | 90 |

Put at a different granularity: four of the six plans are written at a grace period of 90 calendar days and a reinstatement window of 60 calendar days, and the two highest plans, Ridgecrest RxSecure Complete (PDP) and Ridgecrest RxSecure Premier (PDP), are written at 120 and 90 calendar days respectively. A member moving between plans takes the periods of the plan they then hold; the periods are attributes of the plan, never of the member.
